Pactolus.definition: Pactōlus (-los) ī, m , *paktwlo/s, a river of Lydia, with golden sands, V., O.—Prov.: tibi Pactolus fluat, i. e. boundless wealth, H., Iu.

Paeonius.definition: Paeōnius adj., of Paeon (god of physicians), healing, medicinal: herbae, V.: ope Paeoniā, O.

Palatinus.definition: Palātīnus adj., of the Palatium, Palatine: Evander, V.: colles, O.: Apollo (from his temple on the Palatine Hill), H.: laurus, before the imperial palace, O.: cubile, Iu.

Pales.definition: Palēs is, f PA-, an Italian goddess of shepherds and pastures , V., O.

Palilis.definition: Palīlis or Parīlis e, adj. Pales, of Pales : flamma, a fire of straw at the feast of Pales , O.: festa, O.— Plur n . as subst, the feast of Pales, shepherd festival (the 21st of April), C., O.

Pallas.definition: Pallas adis and ados, f , *palla/s, a surname of Athene (identified with the Roman Minerva), V., H., O.: Palladis ales, the owl, O.: Pallados arbor, the olive-tree, O.: iratā Pallade (i. e. invitā M<*>ervā), O.—Oil: i…

Panomphaeus.definition: Panomphaeus ī, m , *panomfai=os, source of all oracles, i. e. Jupiter, O.

Panthoides.definition: Panthoidēs ae, m , *panthoi+/dhs, son of Panthus, Euphorbus, O.—Pythagoras, who claimed that he had been Euphorbus in a previous life, is called Panthoides, H.

Paphius.definition: Paphius adj. , *pa/fios, of Paphos (a city of Cyprus): myrtūs, i. e. sacred to Venus, V.: heros, Cyprian (i. e. Pygmalion), O.

Parca.definition: Parca ae. f PARC-, a goddess of Fate : Parca non mendax, H.: dura, O.—Plur, the Fates (i. e. Klotho, Lachesis, and Atropos), C., H., V., Iu.

Parthenope.definition: Parthenopē ēs, f , *partheno/ph, Neapolis (where the Siren Parthenope was buried), V., O.

Pegasus.definition: Pēgasus (-os) ī, m , *ph/gasos, in fable, a winged horse of the Muses, afterwards a constellation, H., O.—Plur., of swift messengers, C.

Pelasgi.definition: Pelasgī ōrum, m , *pelasgoi/, the Pelasgians, oldest settlers of Greece, V.—The Greeks, V., O.

Penates.definition: Penātēs ium, m 1 PA-, the Penates, guardian gods of the family, household gods : vos Penates patriique di, V., H., O.: deos penatīs salutatum domum Devortar, T.: aedes deorum Penatium, L. — A dwelling, home, hearth (c…

Pergama.definition: Pergama (-mum, Enn. ap. C.), ōrum, n , *pe/rgama, the citadel of Troy, Troy, V., H., O.

Peripateticus.definition: Peripatēticus adj. , *peripathtiko/s, of the Peripatetic philosophy, Aristotelian: philosophi.

Persephone.definition: Persephonē ēs, f , *persefo/nh, Proserpine, O.—Death, Tb., O.

Perses.definition: Persēs ae, m , *pe/rshs, a Persian, C., N.

Persicus.definition: Persicus adj. , *persiko/s, Persian, of Persia: regna, Iu.: apparatūs, i. e. luxurious, H.—Plur n. as subst, Persian history.

Phanaeus.definition: Phanāeus adj. of Phanae (in Chios).—Poet.: rex Phanaeus, i. e. Phanaean wine, V.

Phantasos.definition: Phantasos ī, m , *fa/ntasos, a god of dreams, O.

Pharsalicus.definition: Pharsālicus or Pharsālius adj., Pharsalian, of Pharsalus (in Thessaly).

Philippicus.definition: Philippicus adj. , *filippiko/s, of Philip, Philippic: orationes, Cicero's orations against Antony (in allusion to those of Demosthenes against Philip of Macedon): divina Philippica, i. e. the second Philippic, Iu.

Philippus.definition: Philippus ī, m , *fi/lippos, a king of Macedonia, father of Alexander the Great, C., N.—A gold coin struck by King Philip, H.

Philomela.definition: Philomēla ae, f , *filomh/la, a daughter of Pandion, changed into a nightingale, V., O.—The nightingale, V.

Phlegethon.definition: Phlegethōn ontis, m , *flege/thwn, a river of fire in the Lower World, V.

Phoebas.definition: Phoebas adis, f , *foiba/s, a priestess of Phoebus; hence, an inspired woman, prophetess, O.

Phoebe.definition: Phoebē ēs, f , *foi/bh, goddess of the moon (the Roman Diana), V., O.: tertia, i. e. night, O.

Phoebeius.definition: Phoebēius (O.) or Phoebēus (V., O.), adj., of Phoebus, of Apollo.

Phoebigena.definition: Phoebigena ae, m Phoebus+GEN-, son of Phoebus , i. e. Aesculapius , V.

Phoebus.definition: Phoebus ī, m , *foi/bos, Apollo as the god of light, V., H.—The sun: dum fugat astra Phoebus, H., O.

Phoenissa.definition: Phoenīssa adj. f, *foi/nissa, of Phoenicia (on the Mediterranean Sea): Dido, V.: exul, i. e. Anna, O.—As subst, Dido, V.

Phrygius.definition: Phrygius adj. , *fru/gios, Phrygian, of Phrygia, C., L., V., H., O., Iu.—Plur f. as subst, the Phrygian women, V.—Trojan, of Troy: muri, O.: hymenaei, with Aeneas, V.

Picens.definition: Picēns ntis (C., L.), or Pīcēnus, adj. (S., Cs., C., L., H., Iu.), Picene, of Picenum (in Italy).

Pierius.definition: Pīerius adj. , *pie/rios, Pierian, of Pieria (in Macedonia); hence, Macedonian: paelex, H.—Of the Muses, poetic: antrum, H.: umbra, Iu., H., O., Ph.—Plur f. as subst, the Muses.

Pilumnus.definition: Pīlumnus ī, m pilum, a god of the Latins, who taught how to crush corn , V.

Piraeeus.definition: Pīraeeus (trisyl., C.) or Pīraeus (T., C., Ct., L., N., Pr.), ī, m, or Pīraea, ōrum, n (O.), *peiraieu/s, the port of Athens.

Piraeus.definition: Pīraeus adj., of the Piraeus: litora, O.

Pisaeus.definition: Pīsaeus adj., of Pisa (in Elis), Pisaean: Arethusa, O.: oliva, won in the Olympic games, Iu.

Pleias.definition: Plēïas or Plēas (Plīas) adis, f , *plhi+a/s or *pleia/s, a Pleiad, one of the seven stars, O.— Plur, the Pleiades, Pleiads, V., H., O.

Poecile.definition: Poecilē es, f , *poiki/lh (stoa/), the picture gallery, frescoed hall in the market-place of Athens, N.

Poeni.definition: Poenī ōrum, m the Carthaginians (as of Phoenician origin), C., V.—Sing, the Carthaginian, i. e. Hannibal.—Sing. collect.: Poenus advena, L.: uterque Poenus, i. e. Carthaginians in Africa and Spain, H.

Polyhymnia.definition: Polyhymnia ae, f , *polu/mnia (rich in song), one of the Muses, H., O.

Pomona.definition: Pōmōna ae, f pomum, the goddess of fruit and fruit-trees, Pomona , O.

Porsena.definition: Porsena (C., H.), Porsenna (C., V.), or Porsinna (L.), ae, m a king of Etruria.

Portunus.definition: Portūnus ī, m portus, the god of harbors (the Greek Palaemon), C., V., O.

Priapus.definition: Priāpus ī, m , *pri/apos, Priapus, the god of gardens and vineyards, V., H., O., Iu.: vitreus, a drinking-vessel, Ct.—A lecherous man, O., Ct.

Primigenia.definition: Prīmigenia ae, f primus+GEN-, aboriginal, primal (of Fortuna, as guardian of her favorites from birth), C., L.

Procyon.definition: Procyōn —, m , *proku/wn, the little dog (rising before the dog-star), C., H.

Prometheus.definition: Promētheus (trisyl.), eī (ei, V.), acc. ea, voc. eu, *promhtheu/s (Forethinker), a son of Iapetus, who stole fire from heaven for men, C., H., V., Pr., O., Iu.

Proserpina.definition: Prōserpina (Pros-, H.), ae, f , *persefo/nh, Proserpine, wife of Pluto, and queen of the Lower World, C., V., H., O.: Imperiosa, i. e. death, H.

Puniceus.definition: Pūniceus adj. Punicus, Punic, Carthaginian , O.— Reddish, red, purple-colored : taeniae, V.: rosa, H.: crocus, O.

Punicus.definition: Pūnicus (Poen-) adj. Poeni, Punic, Carthaginian : litterae: fides, i. e. perfidy , S.: perfidia, L.: regna, V.— Of the Phoenician color, purple, purplered : rostra (psittaci), O.: punico Lugubre mutavit sagum, H.

Pygmaeus.definition: Pygmaeus adj., Pygmaean, of the Pygmies (fabulous dwarfs of Africa): mater, i. e. Oenoe, queen of the Pygmies, O.: virgo, a female dwarf, Iu.

Pyrenaeus.definition: Pȳrēnaeus adj., of Pyrene, Pyrenaean: montes, the Pyrenees, Cs., L.: saltus, Cs., L.—As subst m., the Pyrenees, L.

Pythagoricus.definition: Pȳthagoricus (L.), *puthagoriko/s, adj., Pythagorean, of Pythagoras (a philos. of Samos).

Pythicus.definition: Pȳthicus (L.), *puthiko/s, or Pȳthius (C., H., Pr., Iu.), *pu/thios, adj., Pythian, Delphic.

pabulatio.definition: pābulātiō ōnis, f pabulor, a collecting of fodder, foraging : nostrae pabulationes, Cs.: pabulatione intercludi, Cs.

pabulator.definition: pābulātor ōris, m pabulor a forager , Cs., L.

pabulor.definition: pābulor ātus, ārī, dep. pabulum, to forage : angustius, Cs.: pabulandi causā mittere, Cs.: pabulantes (nostros) profligant, Ta.— Supin. acc. : pabulatum cohortes misere, L.

pabulum.definition: pābulum ī, n 1 PA-, food, nourishment, food for cattle, fodder, pasturage, grass : pecoris, S.: secare pabulum, Cs.: comparare, N.: hirundo Pabula parva legens, V.: pabula carpsit ovis, O.: Pabula canescunt, i. e. the…

pacalis.definition: pācālis e, adj. pax, of peace, peaceful : olea, O.: laurus, token of peace , O.: flammae, on the altar of Peace , O.

pacificatio.definition: pācificātiō ōnis, f pacifico, a peace-making, pacification : spes pacificationis.

pacificator.definition: pācificātor ōris, m pacifico, a peace-maker, pacificator : Allobrogum: Athamanum, L.

pacificatorius.definition: pācificātōrius adj. pacificator, peace-making, pacificatory : legatio.

pacifico.definition: (pācificō) —, ātus, āre pacificus, to make peace, conclude peace : Iugurthā pacificante, S.: ad pacificandum stabis, L.— Supin. acc. : legati pacificatum venerunt, L.— To pacify, appease : caelestes pacificasset, Ct.

pacificus.definition: pācificus adj. pax+2 FAC-, peace-making, pacific, peaceable : persona.

paciscor.definition: pacīscor pactus, ī, dep. PAC-, to agree together, bargain, contract, agree, covenant, stipulate, transact : ut ex areā, nisi pactus esset orator, ne tolleret: magnā mercede cum principibus, ut, etc., L.: votis Ne Adda…

paedagogus.definition: paedagōgus ī, m , paidagwgo/s, a governor, preceptor, pedagogue (a slave to guide and attend children), C.—In jest, of an attentive lover, T.

paedico.definition: paedīco —, —, āre, to practice unnatural vice upon, Ct.

paeninsula.definition: paenīnsula (pēn-) ae, f paene+insula, a peninsula , L., Ct.

paenulatus.definition: paenulātus adj. paenula, wearing the paenula, in travelling dress .

paeon.definition: paeōn ōnis, m , paiw/n, a metrical foot of one long and three short syllables (in any order).

paetulus.definition: paetulus adj. dim. paetus with a cast in the eye, slightly blink-eyed .

paetus.definition: paetus adj., with a cast in the eye, blinking, leering, H.

paganus.definition: pāgānus adj. pagus, of the country, of a village, rustic : foci, O.—As subst m., a countryman, peasant, villager, rustic , C.— As subst, a civilian, non-combatant , Iu., Ta.

pagatim.definition: pāgātim adv. pagus, by villages, in every village : templa pagatim sacrata, L.

pagella.definition: pāgella ae, f dim. pagina, a little page .

pagina.definition: pāgina ae, f PAC-, a leaf of paper, sheet, page : hanc paginam tenere: totas paginas commovere: paginas in annalibus magistratuum percurrere, L.: millesima, Iu.: postrema tua, letter. —A slab, tablet : insignis honoru…

paginula.definition: pāginula ae, f dim. pagina, a little page .

pala.definition: pāla ae, f for * pagla; PAC-, a spade : palae innixus, L.— The bezel (of a ring): anuli.

palaestra.definition: palaestra ae, f , palai/stra, a wrestling school, wrestling-place, place of exercise, gymnasium, palaestra: statuas in palaestrā ponere: gramineae palaestrae, V.—A place of discipline in rhetoric, school of rhetoric, …

palaestrita.definition: palaestrīta ae, m , palaistri/ths, a professional wrestler, gymnast.

palea.definition: palea ae, f 1 PAL-, chaff : cum ne paleae quidem relinquerentur: inanes, V.: horna, H.

palimpsestus.definition: palimpsēstus ī, m , pali/myhstos, a parchment rewritten after erasure, palimpsest, C., Ct.

paliurus.definition: paliūrus ī, m , pali/ouros, a plant, Christ'sthorn, V.

palliatus.definition: palliātus adj. pallium, dressed in a pallium (usu. of Greeks): Graeculus iudex: illi palliati, i. e. Grecian statues .

pallidulus.definition: pallidulus adj. dim. pallidus, somewhat pale, rather colorless , Ct., Iu.

pallidus.definition: pallidus adj. with comp. 2 PAL-, pale, pallid, colorless : ut pallidus omnis Cenā desurgat dubiā, H.: hospes pallidior statuā, Ct.: (Dido) morte futurā, V.: recto voltu et pallidus, i. e. well or sick , Iu.: Pallida m…

palliolum.definition: palliolum ī, n dim. pallium, a small Greek mantle, little cloak : sordidum, Caec. ap. C.; Iu.— A hood , O.

pallium.definition: pallium ī, n palla, a cover, coverlet : onerosa pallia iactat, Iu.— A Grecian cloak, mantle : umerum pallio onerare, T.: Pone adprendit pallio, T.: purpureum: cum pallio inambulare, L.

pallor.definition: pallor ōris, m 2 PAL-, pale color, paleness, wanness, pallor : quo tremore et pallore dixit!: albus, H.: gelidus, O.: pallor ora occupat, V.: amantium, H.: tot hominum pallores, the paleness of death , Ta.— Alarm, ter…

palma.definition: palma ae, f , pala/mh, the palm, flat hand: cum manum dilataverat, palmae illius similem, etc.: cavis undam palmis Sustinet, V.: faciem contundere palmā, Iu.—The hand: palmarum intentus: passis palmis salutem petere, …

palmaris.definition: palmāris e, adj. palma, of the palm, superior, excellent : statua.

palmarius.definition: palmārius adj. palma, of the palm, deserving the prize, excellent : sententia.—As subst n., a prize-achievement, masterpiece : palmarium repperisse, T.

palmes.definition: palmes itis, m palma, a young vine-branch, vine-sprig, vine-sprout : laetus, V.: stratus humi palmes, Iu.: caelebs sine palmite truncus, vine , O. — A bough, branch : arborum, Cu.

palmetum.definition: palmētum ī, n palma, a palm-grove.— Plur. : pinguia, H., Ta.

palmifer.definition: palmifer fera, ferum, adj. palma+1 FER-, palm-bearing, abounding in palms , O.

palmosus.definition: palmōsus adj. palma, full of palm-trees , V.

palmula.definition: palmula ae, f dim. palma, an oar-blade, oar , V.

palpito.definition: palpitō —, —, āre, freq. palpo, to tremble, quiver, palpitate : cor palpitat: radix ultima linguae . . . Palpitat, O.

palpo.definition: palpō —, —, āre 1 PAL-, to wheedle, coax : alquem munere, Iu.

paludamentum.definition: palūdāmentum ī, n a military cloak, soldier's cloak: sponsi, L.: paludamenta (consulibus) detracta (as the uniform of generals-in-chief), L.

paludatus.definition: palūdātus adj., with a military cloak, in the garb of a general, in field dress: proficiscebamini paludati in provincias: ut paludati (consules) exeunt, Cs.: lictores, L.: duces, Iu.

paludosus.definition: palūdōsus adj. 2 palus, fenny, boggy, marshy : humus, O.

pampineus.definition: pampineus adj. pampinus, of vine-leaves, of tendrils : vites, O.: auctumnus, V.: hastae, wrapped with vine-leaves , V.: odor, the perfume of wine , Pr.: corona, of vine-leaves , Ta.

pampinus.definition: pampinus ī, m and f PAP-, a tendril of a vine, vine-leaf, vine-foliage : uva vestita pampinis: Ornatus viridi tempora pampino Liber, H.

panacea.definition: panacēa ae, f , pana/keia, an herb said to heal all diseases, all-heal, panacea, catholicon: odorifera, V.

panchrestus.definition: panchrēstus adj. , pa/gxrhstos, good for everything, universally useful: medicamentum, sovereign remedy (i. e. money).

pando.definition: pandō pandī, passus, ere 2 PAT-, to spread out, extend, unfold, expand : ad solem pennas, V.: pictā spectacula caudā, H.: sinūs (i. e. vela), Iu.: panditur planities, extends , L.: dum se cornua latius pandunt, open o…

pandus.definition: pandus adj. PAND-, bent, crooked, curved : carina, V.: rami, O.: cornua, O.: delphines, O.: asellus, crook-backed , O.

panegyricus.definition: panēgyricus adj. , panhguriko/s, of a public assembly, festival.—As subst m. (sc. liber), a festival oration of Isocrates.

pango.definition: pangō pepigī or pēgī (old panxī), pāctus, ere PAC-, to fasten, make fast, fix, drive in : ut clavum pangat, L.—Fig., to make, compose, write, record : maxuma facta patrum, celebrate , Enn. ap. C.: poëmata, H.: de pang…

panicum.definition: pānicum ī, n panis, panic-grass , Cs.

panis.definition: pānis is, m 1 PA-, bread, a loaf : panem in dies mercari, S.: cibarius, coarse bread : secundus, black bread , H.: ater, T.: niveus, Iu.: lapidosus, H.— A loaf, lump, mass : ex hoc effectos panes iaciebant, etc., Cs.

panniculus.definition: panniculus ī, m dim. pannus, a bit of cloth, rag : bombycinus, of silk (as a garment), Iu.

pannosus.definition: pannōsus adj. pannus, ragged, tattered : homines: aedilis, Iu.

pannus.definition: pannus ī, m SPA-, a piece of cloth, garment of cloth : albus, H.: viridis, Iu.— A rag, patch : pannis annisque obsitus, tatters , T.: tenuis, Iu.: Adsuitur pannus, H.: tincti ferrugine panni, O.

panthera.definition: panthēra ae, f , pa/nthhr, a panther, C., L., H., O.

papaver.definition: papāver eris, n a poppy: soporiferum, V.: Lethaeo perfusa papavera somno, V.: summa papaverum capita, poppy-heads, L.

papavereus.definition: papāvereus adj. papaver, of poppies : comae, poppy-flowers , O.

papilio.definition: pāpiliō ōnis, m 1 PAL-, a butterfly, moth , O.

papilla.definition: papilla ae, f dim. papula, a nipple, teat, breast : exserta, V., O., Iu.

papula.definition: papula ae, f dim. PAP-, a pustule, pimple : ardentes, V.

papyrifer.definition: papȳrifer fera, ferum, adj. papyrus+1 FER-, producing papyrus : Nilus, O.: amnis, O.

papyrus.definition: papȳrus ī, f , pa/puros, the paper-plant, paper-reed, papyrus; hence, a garment of papyrus-bark: succinctus patriā papyro, Iu.—Paper (of papyrus-bark), Ct., Iu.

parabilis.definition: parābilis e, adj. paro, easily procured, easy to be had, accessible, at hand : divitiae: victus, Cu.

parasita.definition: parasīta ae, f parasitus, a female parasite , H.

parasitaster.definition: parasītaster trī, m parasitus, a sorry parasite : parvolus, T.

parasitus.definition: parasītus ī, m , para/sitos, a toad-eater, sponge, tuft-hunter, parasite: parasitorum adsentatio: edaces parasiti, H., Iu.

paratio.definition: parātiō ōnis, f 1 paro, a preparing, procuring : regni, compassing the crown , S.

parcus.definition: parcus adj. with comp. and sup. SPAR-, sparing, frugal, thrifty, economical, niggardly, stingy, penurious, parsimonious : colonus parcissimus: parcumque genus patiensque laborum, O.: cui deus obtulit Parcā quod satis …

pardalis.definition: pardalis is, f , pa/rdalis, a female panther, Cu.

pardus.definition: pardus ī, m , pa/rdos, a male panther, Iu.

perbonus.definition: per-bonus adj., very good: agri: perbono loco res erat.

peritia.definition: perītia ae, f peritus, experience, practical knowledge, skill : locorum et militiae, S.: legum, Ta.: peritiā et arte praestans, Ta.

perlabor.definition: per-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to slip through, glide over: in aedem foribus perlapsi angues, L.: Ad nos vix famae perlabitur aura, V.: inde perlapsus ad nos Hercules.

perlaetus.definition: per-laetus adj., very joyful: supplicatio, L.

perlateo.definition: per-lateō uī, —, ēre, to remain hidden, O.

perlego.definition: per-legō or pellegō lēgī, lēctus, ere, to view all over, examine thoroughly, scan, survey: omnia oculis, V.: dispositas per atria ceras, O.—To read through, peruse: perlectis litteris, S.: perlectam (epistulam), recit…

perlevis.definition: per-levis e, adj., very slight, trifling: perlevi momento fortunae pendēre, C., L.

perliberalis.definition: per-līberālis e, adj., very well bred, T.

perlito.definition: per-litō āvī, ātus, āre, to offer sacrifices till favorable omens appear: bove, L.: primis hostiis perlitatum est, i. e. the first victims yielded favorable auspices, L.: diu non perlitatum tenuerat dictatorem, the lo…

perluceo.definition: per-lūceō (pell-) lūxī, —, ēre, to shine through, glimmer: perlucens iam aliquid lux, i. e. in some measure piercing, L.: pelluces, i. e. you wear a transparent garment, Iu.— P. praes., transparent: perlucens aether: …

perluo.definition: per-luō uī, ūtus, ere, to wash off, wash, bathe, lave: manūs puras undā, O.: perluitur solitā Titania lymphā, bathes, O.: in fluminibus perlui, Cs.

perlustro.definition: per-lūstrō āvī, ātus, āre, to go over, wander all through, traverse completely: hostium agros, L.—Fig., to view all over, examine, survey: materia perlustranda animo: omnia oculis, L.

permagnus.definition: per-māgnus adj., very great, vast, immense: hereditas: numerus, Cs.: tua res permagna agitur, interests: negotia, H.—As subst n., a very great thing: permagnum existimans (with acc. and infin.): permagni interest, it …

permaneo.definition: per-maneō mānsī, mānsūrus, ēre, to stay, hold out, last, continue, abide, be permanent, endure, remain, persist, persevere: ut quam maxime permaneant diuturna corpora: ira tam permansit diu, T.: quis confidit illud st…

permano.definition: per-mānō āvī, —, āre. to flow to, penetrate, reach: sucus permanat ad iecur: (venenum) in omnis partīs corporis.—Fig., to penetrate, reach, extend to: ne ad patrem hoc permanet, reach the ears of, T.: macula permanat …

permansio.definition: permānsiō ōnis, f per+1 MAN-, a remaining, abiding : quodvis supplicium levius est hac permansione, than abiding here.— A persistence : in unā sententiā: in ratione.

permarinus.definition: per-marīnus adj., escorting through the sea: Lares, guardian gods of voyagers, L.

permaturesco.definition: per-mātūrēscō ruī, —, ere, inch, to ripen fully: pomum, ubi permaturuit, O.

permediocris.definition: per-mediocris e, adj., very moderate: motus.

permeo.definition: per-meō —, —, āre, to go over, pass through, cross, traverse: maria ac terras, O.: longius in hostes, Ta.— Fig., to penetrate, pervade: (intellegentia) per omnia.

permetior.definition: per-mētior mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure through, measure out, measure: solis magnitudinem: permenso tempore lucis, i. e. at the end of life, Tb.—To traverse: classibus aequor, V.

permingo.definition: per-mingō mīnxī, —, ere, to make water upon, abuse, H.

permirus.definition: per-mīrus adj., very wonderful, amazing: illud vero mihi permirum accidit, fuisse, etc.—In tmesi: per mihi mirum visum est.

permisceo.definition: per-misceō miscuī, mīxtus, ēre, to mix together, mix thoroughly, commingle, intermingle: equites pedites permixti, S.: naturam cum materiā: permixti cum suis fugientibus, Cs.: permixtum senatui populi concilium, L.: g…

permissio.definition: permissiō ōnis, f permitto, a yielding, surrender at discretion : extra civium corpora, L.— Leave, permission : mea permissio mansionis tuae.

permitto.definition: per-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to let pass, let go, let loose: equos in hostem, i. e. ride at full speed, L.—To let go, reach with, cast, hurl: saxum in hostem, O.—Fig., to let loose, let go: tribunatum, exercise withou…

permixtio.definition: permīxtiō ōnis, f per+MIC-, a mixing together, mixture , C.— A confusion, disturbance : terrae, S.

permodestus.definition: per-modestus adj., very modest, extremely shy: homo: verba sensu permodesto, moderate, Ta.

permolo.definition: per-molō —, —, ere, to grind thoroughly: uxores, H.

permotio.definition: per-mōtiō ōnis, f per+1 MV-, a moving, exciting, excitement : mentis: permotionis causā, to stir the feelings.—An emotion : permotiones animis datae.

permoveo.definition: per-moveō mōvī, mōtus, ēre, to move deeply, rouse, excite, agitate, influence, lead, induce, prevail on: quem res tanta non permovet, S.: maxime hac re permovebantur, quod, etc., were most influenced, Cs.: ne animo pe…

permulceo.definition: per-mulceō mulsī, mulsus, ēre, to rub gently, stroke: manu eum, O.: barbam, L.—To touch gently: aram flatu permulcet spiritus austri, blows softly upon, C. poët.: medicata lumina virgā, O.— Fig., to soothe, charm, ple…

permultus.definition: per-multus adj., very much, very many: imitatores: colles, Cs.—As subst n.: permultum erit ex maerore tuo diminutum: permulta rogatus Fecit, H.

permunio.definition: per-mūniō īvī, ītus, īre, to finish fortifying, fortify thoroughly: quae munimenta incohaverat, L.: castris permunitis, L.

permutatio.definition: permūtātiō ōnis, f permuto, a change, alteration, revolution, crisis : magna rerum: temporum.— An interchanging, barter, exchange : captivorum, L.: mercium, Ta.: quae (pecunia) mihi ex publicā permutatione debetur, a …

permuto.definition: per-mūtō āvī, ātus, āre, to change throughout, alter completely: omnem rei p. statum.—To interchange, exchange: captivos, L.: galeam, V.: valle Sabinā divitias, H.—Of money, to exchange, pay by bill of exchange: illud…

perna.definition: perna ae, f , pe/rna, a haunch, ham with the leg, gammon: fumosa cum pede, H.

pernecessarius.definition: per-necessārius adj., very necessary, pressing: tempus.— Very closely connected, very intimate: amicus: homo mihi.—As subst m.: Leptae nostri: paternus.

pernego.definition: per-negō āvī, —, āre, to deny stoutly: alqd, T.: saepe appellati, pernegaverunt.

perniciabilis.definition: perniciābilis e, adj. pernicies, destructive, ruinous : nix oculis, Cu.: morbi, L.

pernicies.definition: perniciēs (not-tiēs), acc. em (gen. once iī, C.; dat. once iē, L., once iī, N.), f per+1 NEC-, destruction, death, ruin, overthrow, disaster, calamity, mischief : instructa ad perniciem, T.: senatoribus perniciem mach…

perniciosus.definition: perniciōsus adj. with comp. and sup. pernicies, destructive, ruinous, baleful, pernicious : lubido, S.: flamma: leges, Cs.: scripta auctori perniciosa suo, O.: morbi perniciosiores: Obsequium ventris mihi perniciosius…

pernicitas.definition: pernīcitās ātis, f pernix, nimbleness, briskness, agility, swiftness : electi (milites) ad pernicitatem, Cs.: adde pernicitatem: pedum, L.

perniciter.definition: pernīciter adv. pernix, nimbly, swiftly : desilire, L.: exsilire, Ct.

pernix.definition: pernīx īcis, adj. per+CNI-, persistent, persevering : iacet (taurus) instrato saxa cubili, V.— Nimble, brisk, active, agile, quick, swift, fleet : corpora exercitatione, L.: virgo pernicibus ignea plantis, V.: puella,…

pernobilis.definition: per-nōbilis e, adj., very famous: epigramma.

pernocto.definition: per-noctō āvī, ātūrus, āre, to stay all night, pass the night: foris, T.: ibi: extra moenia, L.: pro me pernoctet epistula tecum, O.: haec studia pernoctant nobiscum.

pernosco.definition: per-nōscō nōvī, nōtus, ere, to examine thoroughly: pernoscite, Furtumne factum existimetis, T.— To learn thoroughly, become fully acquainted with: non satis alqm, T.: rem cognoscite, Ut pernoscatis, etc., T.: motūs an…

pernotesco.definition: pernōtēscō tuī, ere, inch, to become generally known: ubi incolumem esse pernotuit, Ta.

pernox.definition: per-nox noctis, adj., through the night, all night: (bos) iacet pernox instrato cubili, V. (al. pernix): luna, full, L.: lunā pernocte, by the full moon, O.: luditur alea pernox, Iu.

pernumero.definition: per-numerō āvī, ātus, āre, to count out, reckon up: pecuniam, L.

pero.definition: pērō ōnis, m a long laced boot of raw hide (for soldiers and wagoners), V., Iu.

perobscurus.definition: per-obscūrus adj., very obscure: quaestio: fama, L.

perofficiose.definition: per-officiōsē adv., very serviceably, with devotion: me observare.

peropportunus.definition: per-opportūnus adj., very seasonable, most opportune: diversorium: victoria, L.

peroptato.definition: per-optātō adv. optatus, exactly as desired : peroptato nobis datum est.

peropus.definition: per-opus adv., very necessary: peropus est, hunc cum ipsā loqui, T.

peroratio.definition: perōrātiō ōnis, f peroro, a summing up, peroration : eius.

perorno.definition: per-ōrnō āvi, —, āre, to adorn constantly: senatum, Ta.

peroro.definition: per-ōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to speak from beginning to end, plead throughout, harangue at length: a Quinto causa est Sesti perorata: breviter peroratum esse, L.: In Proculas, Iu.—To end, close, conclude, finish: strepitu …

perosus.definition: perōsus P. dep. per-odi, detesting, hating greatly, weary of, disgusted with : lucem, V.: genus omne Femineum, V.: Creten, O.: superbiam regis, L.: decemvirorum scelera, L.

perpaco.definition: per-pācō —, ātus, āre, to quiet completely, pacify thoroughly: omnibus perpacatis, L.

perparvus.definition: per-parvus (-vos) adj., very little, trifling, minute: navigium: culpa.—As subst n.: perparvum ex illis lucris.

perpaulus.definition: per-paulus adj., very little.—As subst n., a very little: loci.

perpello.definition: per-pellō pulī, —, ere, to drive, urge, force, compel, constrain, prevail upon: ad deditionem, L.: orare, usque adeo, donec perpulit, carried his point, T.: Aulum spe pactionis, ut, etc., S.: decemviros, ut, etc., L.:…

perpendiculum.definition: perpendiculum ī, n perpendo, a plummet, plumb-line : ad perpendiculum columnas exigere, set by plummet : ad perpendiculum, perpendicularly : non directe ad perpendiculum, sed prone, Cs.

perpendo.definition: per-pendō pendī, —, ere, to weigh carefully, examine, ponder, consider: momenta officiorum: amicitia, quae tota veritate perpenditur, is valued altogether according to its truth.

perpessio.definition: perpessiō ōnis, f perpetior, a bearing, suffering, endurance : harum rerum: laborum.

perpetior.definition: perpetior pessus, ī, dep. per+patior, to bear steadfastly, suffer firmly, stand out, abide, endure, be patient : contumelias, T.: inperia saeva, S.: o multa dictu gravia, perpessu aspera: supplicium, Cs.: mihi omnia p…

perpetro.definition: per-petrō āvī, ātus, āre per+patro, to carry through, complete, effect, achieve, execute, perform, accomplish, commit, perpetrate : ut Ilenses munere solverentur, Ta.—Usu. P. pass. : suo labore perpetratum, ne, etc., …

perpetuitas.definition: perpetuitās ātis, f perpetuus, uninterrupted duration, continuous succession, continuity, perpetuity : philosophi spectandi sunt ex perpetuitate atque constantiā, i. e. general tenor and system : ad perpetuitatem, for…

perpetuus.definition: per-petuus adj. per+1 PAT-, continuous, unbroken, uninterrupted, constant, entire, whole, perpetual : agmen: vigiliaeque stationesque, a continuous line of , etc., Cs.: Perpetuis soliti patres considere mensis, V.: in…

perplaceo.definition: per-placeō —, —, ēre, to please greatly: ea (lex) mihi perplacet.

perplexus.definition: per-plexus adj. with comp, interwoven, entangled, involved, intricate: iter silvae, V.: carmen perplexius, L.—Fig., intricate, unintelligible, ambiguous, obscure, inscrutable: sermones, L.: responsum, L.—As subst n., …

perpolio.definition: per-poliō īvī, ītus, īre, to polish thoroughly, finish, make perfect: opus: ea, quae habes instituta: perpoliendi labor.

perpopulor.definition: per-populor ātus, āre, dep., to lay waste utterly, devastate, pillage completely: Italiam, L.: perpopulato agro, L.: homines, Ta.

perpotatio.definition: perpōtātiō ōnis, f perpoto, a drinking-bout : intemperantissimae perpotationes.

perpoto.definition: per-pōtō āvī, —, āre, to keep drinking, tipple, carouse: totos dies: ad vesperum: perpotandi dulcedo, Cu.

perprimo.definition: perprimō —, —, ere per+premo, to press hard, press perpetually : cubilia, lie upon , H.

perpropinquus.definition: per-propinquus adj., very near: commutatio rerum, Att. ap. C.—As subst m., a very near relation: Auri.

perpulcher.definition: per-pulcher (-cer) chra, chrum, adj., very beautiful: dona, T.

perpurgo.definition: per-pūrgō (old perpūrigō) ā vī, ātus, āre, to cleanse thoroughly, purge: se quādam herbulā.— Fig., to clear up, explain: locus orationis perpurgatus ab iis: de dote tanto magis, arrange.

perpusillus.definition: per-pusillus adj., very small, very little: perpusillum rogabo (in a double sense adj. or adv. ), I will ask very little, or, the very little man.

perquam.definition: per-quam or per quam adv., as much as possible, extremely, exceedingly, T.: perquam grave est dictu: pauci, L.: breviter: per pol quam paucos reperias, T.

perquiro.definition: perquīrō —, quīsītus, ere per+quaero, to ask diligently after, make eager search for : vasa: vias in Suevos, Cs.: raptam, O.: non perquiris, cui dixit Apronius?: cognitionem rei, investigate .

perreconditus.definition: per-reconditus adj., most abstruse: ratio consuetudinis.

perrepo.definition: per-rēpō —, —, ere, to crawl over: tellurem genibus, Tb.

perrepto.definition: per-rēptō āvī, —, āre, freq, to creep over, crawl through: usque omne oppidum, T.

perridiculus.definition: per-rīdiculus adj., very laughable, highly absurd: doctrina.

perrogo.definition: per-rogō —, —, āre, to ask in succession, complete the roll-call: perrogari sententiae non potuere, the voting could not be finished, L.

perrumpo.definition: per-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break through, force a way through, get across: per medios hostīs, Cs.: in vestibulum templi, L.: nec per castra perrumpi posse, L.: paludem, Cs.: perrumpitur concretus aër: bipenni Lim…

persaepe.definition: per-saepe adv., very often: quod persaepe fit, C., H.

persalutatio.definition: persalūtātiō ōnis, f persaluto, a general salutation, greeting of everybody .

persaluto.definition: per-salūtō āvī, ātus, āre, to salute in succession: omnīs: deos, Ph.: a toto exercitu persalutatus est, Cu.

persapiens.definition: per-sapiēns entis, adj., very wise: homo.

perscindo.definition: per-scindō —, —, ere, to rend asunder, tear in pieces: omnia perscindente vento, L.

perscribo.definition: per-scrībō īpsī, īptus, ere, to write in full, write at length, write out: res gestas populi R., S.: de meis rebus ad Lollium: hoc perscriptum in monumentis reperietis, ut, etc.: a primordio urbis res populi R., L.: v…

perscriptio.definition: perscrīptiō ōnis, f perscribo, a writing down, entry, official record : perscriptionum et liturarum adversaria: illud senatūs consultum eā perscriptione est, ut, etc., i. e. of such a tenor.—A making over by writing, …

perscriptor.definition: perscrīptor ōris, m perscribo, a book-keeper, accountant : faenerationis.

perscrutor.definition: per-scrūtor ātus, ārī, dep., to search through, examine, scrutinize: castelli planitiem, S.: (canes) perscrutabantur omnia.—Fig., to examine into, investigate: rationem criminum.

perseco.definition: per-secō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut up, extirpate, cut out: id (vitium), L.: rerum naturas, lay bare: perseca et confice, cut away (obstacles).

persedeo.definition: per-sedeō (-sideō) —, —, ēre, to remain sitting, sit continuously: totā nocte in speculis, Cu.: in equo persedendo, L.

persegnis.definition: per-sēgnis e, adj., very sluggish: proelium, L.

persentio.definition: per-sentiō sī, —, īre, to feel deeply: pectore curas, V.—To apprehend clearly, perceive distinctly: eam tali peste teneri, V.

persentisco.definition: per-sentīscō —, —, intens, to perceive clearly, detect: id, T.: Quot res dedere, T.

persequor.definition: per-sequor cūtus or quūtus, ī, dep., to follow perseveringly, follow after, follow up, pursue: certum est persequi, T.: me in Asiam, T.: exercitum: Hortensium ipsius vestigiis: alcuius vestigia: te, V.: Hanc persecuta…

perseveranter.definition: persevēranter adv. with comp. perseverans, perseveringly : tueri, L.: perseverantius saevire, L.

perseverantia.definition: persevērantia ae, f persevero, steadfastness, perseverance : eius nimia, obstinacy : sententiae tuae: nautarum, Cs.

persevero.definition: persevērō āvī, ātus, āre perseverus, to abide, adhere strictly, continue steadfastly, persist, persevere : (navis) perseveravit, kept on its course , Cs.: in suā sententiā: in vitiis: in eo, ius publicano non dicere: …

perseverus.definition: per-sevērus adj., very strict: imperium, Ta.

persido.definition: per-sīdō sēdī, —, ere, to sink down, penetrate: Altius ad vivum, V.

persigno.definition: per-sīgnō —, —, āre, to register accurately, record: triumviri donis persignandis, L.

persimilis.definition: per-similis e, adj., very like, precisely similar: statua istius: isti tabulae liber, H.

persimplex.definition: per-simplex icis, adj., very simple: victus, Ta.

persisto.definition: per-sistō —, —, ere, to abide, persist: in impudentiā, L.—(For perf. system see persto).

persolvo.definition: per-solvō solvī, solūtus, ere, to unravel, solve, explain: hoc mihi.—To pay, pay out, pay over: pretium tibi, T.: pecuniam a discipulis suis Fufiis, pay by a draft on, etc.: (aes alienum) alienis nominibus suis copiis…

persona.definition: persōna ae, f per+SON-, a mask, false face (usu. of clay or bark, covering the head; worn by actors): tragica, Ph.: pallens, Iu.: mulier videtur, Non persona loqui, i. e. no man disguised , Iu.— An assumed character, …

personatus.definition: persōnātus adj. persona, in a mask, masked : Roscius: pater, i. e. in the play , H.—Fig.: cur personatus ambulem, in an assumed character .

persono.definition: per-sonō uī, —, āre, to sound through and through, resound, fill with sound, reëcho: cum domus cantu personaret: domus Personuit canibus, H.: totis castris, to be heard, L.: ab aetherio personat axe fragor, O.: cithar…

perspergo.definition: perspergō —, spersas, ere per+spargo, to besprinkle, tinge : unde haustā aquā templum perspersum, Ta.— Fig.: quo tamquam sale perspergatur oratio.

perspicax.definition: perspicāx ācis, adj. per+SPEC-, sharpsighted, penetrating, acute, perspicacious : prudentia: homo, T.: ad has res, T.: alqd naturā.

perspicio.definition: perspiciō spēxī, spectus, ere SPEC-, to look through, look into, look at, see through : quo ne perspici quidem posset, Cs.: eas (epistulas), look through : ut prae densitate arborum perspici caelum vix posset, be disc…

perspicuitas.definition: perspicuitās ātis, f perspicuus, clearness, perspicuity .

perspicuus.definition: perspicuus adj. SPEC-, transparent, clear : aquae, O.— Fig., evident, clear, manifest, perspicuous : mors: consilia: hoc inter omnī s.

persterno.definition: per-sternō —, strātus, ere, to pave throughout: via a silice perstrata est, L.

perstimulo.definition: per-stimulō —, —, āre, to stimulate violently: spiritūs, Ta.

persto.definition: per-stō stitī, statūrus, āre, to stand firmly, continue standing, remain unmoved: diem totum, L.: in limine, Tb.: (Symplegades) inmotae perstant, O.—To remain unchanged, last, endure, abide: nihil est toto quod perste…

perstrepo.definition: per-strepō —, ere, to make much noise, T.

perstringo.definition: per-stringō inxī, ictus, ere, to bind closely, press hard, touch closely, graze: femur, V.: solum aratro, plough slightly: vomere portam, graze against: uterum perstrinxerat arbor, had overgrown, O.: murmure aures, de…

perstudiosus.definition: per-studiōsus adj., very desirous, extremely fond: musicorum: litterarum.

persuadeo.definition: per-suādeō suāsī, suāsus, ēre, to convince, persuade: homo factus ad persuadendum: hoc persuadere, non interire animas, Cs.: velim tibi ita persuadeas, me, etc.: de paupertate: hoc tibi vere, H.: si scit et persuasus …

persuasio.definition: persuāsiō ōnis, f SVAD-, a convincing, conviction : dicere apposite ad persuasionem: super<*> stitionum persuasione, Ta.

persubtilis.definition: per-subtīlis e, adj., very ingenious: oratio.

persulto.definition: persultō āvī, —, āre per + salto, to leap about, prance, range through : in agro, L.: silvas, scour , Ta.

pertaedet.definition: (per-taedet) taesum est, ēre, impers, it wearies, disgusts, makes sick: Si non pertaesum thalami fuisset, i. e. had I not come to hate marriage, V.: pertaesum est enim (me) levitatis: negoti eum, N.

pertendo.definition: per-tendō tendī, —, ere, to press on, carry out, continue: Verum si incipies, neque pertendes naviter, T.: ut coeperam hoc, T.: pertendens animo, stubborn, Pr.—To push on, proceed: Romam, L.

pertenuis.definition: per-tenuis e, adj., extremely slight, very weak: spes salutis: suspicio: argumentum: ars.

perterebro.definition: per-terebrō āvī, —, āre, to bore through.

pertergeo.definition: per-tergeō tersī, —, ēre, to wipe off, wipe dry: Gausape mensam, H.

perterrefacio.definition: perterrēfaciō —, —, ere perterreo+facio, to frighten thoroughly : Davom, T.

perterreo.definition: per-terreō —, itus, ēre, to frighten thoroughly, terrify: hunc, T.: alios magnitudine poenarum, Cs.: metu perterriti: caede viri perterrita agmina, V.: malefici conscientiā perterritus.

perterricrepus.definition: perterricrepus adj. perterreo+CRAP-, rattling terribly , Poët. ap. C.

pertica.definition: pertica ae, f a pole, long staff: longa, O.—A signal pole, Cu.—A measuring rod, Pr.

pertimesco.definition: per-timēscō muī, —, ere, inch, to be frightened, be alarmed, fear greatly: Catilina ipse pertimuit: de fortunis suis: cuiusquam vim: legatum, S.: nomen imperi etiam in levi personā pertimescitur: ne quid peccasset: qu…

pertinacia.definition: pertinācia ae, f pertinax, perseverance, persistence, stubbornness, obstinacy, pertinacity : perseverantiae finitima: hominum nimia, Cs.: pertinaciae finem facere, Cs.: iusta, L.— Person., C.

pertinax.definition: pertināx ācis, adj. with comp. and sup. per+ tenax, persevering, unyielding, obstinate, pertinacious, stubborn : pertinacissimus fueris, si, etc.: virtus, L.: concertationes in disputando: pertinacior in repugnando, L…

pertineo.definition: pertineō uī, —, ēre per+teneo; to stretch out, reach, extend : venae in omnīs partīs corporis pertinentes: deus pertinens per naturam cuiusque rei: Belgae pertinent ad partem fluminis, Cs.— Fig., to reach, extend : ea…
